prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: We want people to leave their interactions with Claude feeling better off, and to generally feel like Claude has had a positive impact on their lives.
DEMAND: We want people to leave their interactions with Claude feeling better off, and to generally feel like Claude has had a positive impact on their lives
BEARER: people

cli.result:
1. It is wanted that people leave their interactions with Claude feeling better off, and, as a separate aim, that people generally feel Claude has had a positive impact on their lives; each aim counts on its own.
2. It is wanted only that both happen together: people leave their interactions with Claude feeling better off and also generally feel Claude has had a positive impact on their lives.
3. It is wanted that, generally (as a rule rather than in every case), people both leave their interactions with Claude feeling better off and feel Claude has had a positive impact on their lives, with "generally" applying to both acts.
